exposes_tools.name: market.quote
exposes_tools.description: Current price of one asset, in the currency this plugin determined that price is in. This tool never converts: it answers one asset's price in one market's currency, and conversion happens only where a portfolio is totalled. Callers name the asset AND its venue; which source answers a venue, at which URL, is chosen by this plugin. Neither source states a currency, so it is determined from the venue and the code range: CRYPTO in USDT, US in USD, HK in HKD below code 80000, and in CNY the Shanghai 6xxxxx (A shares and STAR) and 5xxxxx (funds) codes and the Shenzhen 00xxxx (main board), 30xxxx (ChiNext) and 15xxxx/16xxxx (fund) codes. Codes outside those ranges — B shares, Hong Kong's renminbi and US-dollar counters, and the mainland bond and index ranges — are refused with the reason rather than priced under a guessed currency.

asset.description: Asset name. Bare (`BTC`) means the crypto venue; a venue-qualified name is `<VENUE>:<SYMBOL>` over CRYPTO, US, HK, SH (Shanghai) and SZ (Shenzhen) — `CRYPTO:BTC`, `US:NVDA`, `HK:1810`, `SH:600519`, `SZ:000001`. A prefix counts only with the colon, so `USNVDA` is a crypto name. `CN:` is accepted only so holdings stored under the retired mainland venue still read back; it is never priced, and has to be re-recorded under the exchange that lists the code — `SH:<code>` for a Shanghai listing, `SZ:<code>` for a Shenzhen one, not whichever is convenient. A Hong Kong code folds to five zero-padded digits, so `HK:1810` and `HK:01810` are one holding.

exposes_tools.name: market.holdings.set
exposes_tools.description: Record how much of an asset this Track holds. Replaces any existing quantity for that asset; 0 removes it. Records only — the price is fetched by the plugin's own refresh, which this call wakes. Each venue is priced in its own currency, and the total is stated in the settlement currency the install configures (USD or CNY), converted at rates read from the same quote source. A holding whose rate could not be read this pass keeps its own price but has no converted value, is left out of the total, and stops that tick contributing a history point.

asset.description: Asset name. Bare (`BTC`) means the crypto venue; a venue-qualified name is `<VENUE>:<SYMBOL>` over CRYPTO, US, HK, SH (Shanghai) and SZ (Shenzhen) — `CRYPTO:BTC`, `US:NVDA`, `HK:1810`, `SH:600519`, `SZ:000001`. A prefix counts only with the colon, so `USNVDA` is a crypto name. `CN:` is accepted only so holdings stored under the retired mainland venue still read back; it is never priced, and has to be re-recorded under the exchange that lists the code — `SH:<code>` for a Shanghai listing, `SZ:<code>` for a Shenzhen one, not whichever is convenient. A Hong Kong code folds to five zero-padded digits, so `HK:1810` and `HK:01810` are one holding.

quantity.description: How much is held. 0 removes the holding.

exposes_tools.name: market.holdings.list
exposes_tools.description: What this Track currently holds, with the venue, the latest price in its own market's currency, the rate applied and the value in the settlement currency. When every holding priced and converted, the reply states the total; when some did not, it states a partial total and says it covers only the holdings that did. If the configured settlement currency is unsupported, values remain in their native currencies: counted holdings in one currency still have a total, while counted holdings spanning currencies do not. There is also no total when nothing could be valued or when the values do not sum to a finite number — the reply says which. The rate behind each conversion is named in the prose and in `conversions`, including the one step that is an assumption rather than a quote (USDT is taken as 1 USD); the per-row `rate` is a bare number and does not distinguish the two.

exposes_tools.name: market.cash.set
exposes_tools.description: Record this Track's current absolute fiat cash balance. Replaces the amount for one currency; zero remains a recorded zero. Whole cents only; never a deposit, trade or automatic cash deduction. Saves only and queues a portfolio refresh; no pricing/network in this tool.

amount.description: Current absolute balance in whole cents, e.g. 0.29 or 100000. Sub-cent or unsafe-range values are refused without rounding.

exposes_tools.name: market.cash.list
exposes_tools.description: Read this Track's saved native cash balances without fetching prices or exchange rates. Empty means no cash recorded; an explicit zero is retained. Use to confirm the outcome after an indeterminate write.

quote.description: The currency a portfolio's total is stated in. Two values settle: USD and CNY. USDT is accepted and settles as USD, which is what the default means and what every install that never set this key gets; the USDT-to-USD step is an assumed parity of 1, not a quoted rate (the pair answered 0.99967 on 2026-09-07, so the approximation is about 3.3 basis points on the USDT-quoted part of a portfolio). Any other value, HKD included, settles nothing: each holding keeps its own market's currency, and a portfolio spanning two of them gets no total. A price is never converted: every price this plugin publishes is the number its own market quoted. What is converted is each holding's VALUE, and with it the total, at rates read from the quote source; a rate that cannot be read leaves its holdings without a value and out of the total, rather than being carried over from an earlier pass.

binance_endpoint.description: Base URL of the Binance market-data source. api.binance.com is geo-restricted from some hosts; data-api.binance.vision serves the same /api/v3 paths with no key.

sina_endpoint.description: Base URL of the Sina quote list, the US, HK, SH and SZ source. Its /list= path is asked for one symbol at a time: gb_<symbol>, hk<5-digit code>, sh<code> or sz<code>.
